H1.note: Friction: retaliation and staged release hold under stable and fail under turnover (both benchmarks: 0 vs 1).

H2.note: Agency: under turnover the bonus restores compliance where retaliation, staged release and collateral fail.

H3.note: Insurance: collateral x turnover fails to deter; both benchmarks have A, not B, end the deal (benchmark mean scores A 150, B 180 at g=10).

H4.note: Attribution: under renaming B must freeze every A worker to deter; innocents absorb freezes after any breach.

H5.note: Placebo: renaming should not change staged release, collateral or the bonus. Haiku: a floor effect (0 overdraws in every stable and renaming cell), so the test is uninformative for Haiku; Luna is the real test of H5.

H7.note: Infrastructure: the gateway holds under turnover plus renaming. Note the comparison is gateway x infrastructure against the other mechanisms x turnover: there is no infrastructure-without-gateway cell, so the design cannot separate the gateway from the infrastructure condition itself.

H8.note: Strategic, not noise: raising g from 10 to 30. Per_worker predicts a flip in every cell that complies at g=10; contest_aware predicts a flip only in the h8_noise_check cells (bonus x turnover, gateway x infrastructure). Haiku: overdraw rises with g in 5/5 turnover/infrastructure cells (round 1; all rounds 5/5) and in 0/8 stable/renaming cells (round 1; all rounds 2/8).

H6.note: Choice (Exp 2/3, Haiku only). The bonus result rests on 2 proposals (both rejected): insufficient data. Freezes are not rarer under renaming than under stable (15/60 vs 17/60), so adaptation away from retaliation is not supported. The gateway was proposed in 60/60 infrastructure trials, which may reflect salience (it is the only option named after the condition's infrastructure) rather than strategic adaptation.
